scope: Chrome 153 production-browser recovery of the public MPEG-TS-to-AVI packet-copy route at its 199649420-byte published maximum

browser.name: Chrome
browser.memoryFormula: peak complete Chromium process-tree private memory during conversion - stable clean blank-Chromium process-tree private memory

rejectedBaseline.failure: All three runs exceeded the unchanged 250 MiB limit, despite genuine repeatable output and cancellation cleanup.
rejectedBaseline.peakProcessDiagnosis: The peak sample had a 270.26 MiB renderer, a 109.52 MiB GPU process, and two conversion-related worker realms.

acceptedTopology.directSave: Quota-preflighted synchronous browser-private stage followed by one backpressured 256 KiB copy to the selected destination; staging deleted on success, cancellation, write failure, or worker crash.
acceptedTopology.opfsTest: Existing synchronous OPFS writer without an additional final copy.

opfsAcceptedSessions.cancellation: at destination-open with zero output bytes; valid but weaker than the subsequent active-work probe

failedTestHarnessProbe.reason: The profiler waited for a staged final-copy phase in OPFS mode, which does not stage; the conversion completed before that impossible checkpoint. The corrected harness passed, then passed again with cancellation after 8141744 actual output bytes.

focusedProductionBrowserChecks.genuineSmallConversion: MPEG-TS to genuine AVI passed independent FFprobe, exact compressed packets, decoded-video equality, and complete native decode.
focusedProductionBrowserChecks.injectedFinalCopyWriteFailure: Error surfaced, at most one pending bounded write, partial destination removed, and no stage remained.
focusedProductionBrowserChecks.injectedWorkerCrash: A first run found staging left behind when the terminated worker's OPFS lock had not yet released. The cleanup now retries removal before restart; the corrected MPEG-TS-to-AVI and pre-existing MP4-to-AVI crash tests both passed with no stage or partial destination.

speedDecision: For the identical source and byte-identical output, the accepted path's nine-run median was 4.48717 seconds versus 48.730815 seconds for the rejected direct writer's three-run median, a 10.86x median improvement. The accepted route also lowered the observed worst complete-browser incremental private memory by 45.7109375 MiB.
limitations: The worst direct-save run left only 1.671875 MiB of measured headroom on this Chrome version and machine, not a cross-machine guarantee. Browser-private staging temporarily consumes one output-sized amount of disk space before deletion.
